nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite abelian group of odd order, written additively, and let $A, B \subseteq G$ be subsets with $|A| = |B|$. Then there is a bijection $f \colon A \to B$ such that the sums $a + f(a)$, for $a \in A$, are pairwise distinct.
nodes.title: Snevily's conjecture is true

nodes.summary: The statement that for every finite abelian group $G$ of odd order, written additively, and all subsets $A, B \subseteq G$ with $|A| = |B|$, there is a bijection $f \colon A \to B$ such that the sums $a + f(a)$, for $a \in A$, are pairwise distinct.
nodes.title: Snevily's conjecture
